brief: Deutsche Bank argues growth is the single factor explaining 2026's market conditions: high yields (driven almost exclusively by neutral rates), equities near record highs, tight credit and low cross-asset volatility. The growth driver is an unprecedented global capex cycle, powered by AI investment plus a government-financed buildout of strategic autonomy across industries. Historically, capex booms excluding WWII reconstruction are rare: only two comparable episodes, the late 1980s and mid-2000s (dotcom does not rank in the top five), averaging 3 years in duration. DB estimates the current boom could run 5 years, contributing a cumulative 3% to GDP under conservative assumptions or 6% under optimistic ones, making it the second-largest post-reconstruction boom either way. Global data surprises are on track for their largest positive run on record, and DB argues consensus underappreciates the cycle's resilience and acyclicality. Because past capex booms coincided with gradual dollar weakening, DB's FX Blueprint has argued against a large dollar breakout this year, and DB would not chase the dollar higher after the recent repricing.
